prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Emoji · 服务状态 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "服务" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 87px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 54px
  col 3: header "可用率" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 54px
  col 4: header "最近事件" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 387px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [82, 76, 76, 125] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [81, 75, 75, 128] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [83, 75, 75, 126] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [83, 76, 75, 125] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [84, 75, 75, 125] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [82, 75, 75, 127] · table 360×428px · row heights [36, 60, 106, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [108, 75, 75, 101] · table 360×521px · row heights [36, 36, 153, 83, 129, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [82, 78, 75, 124] · table 360×451px · row heights [36, 60, 129, 60, 106, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r2A","r2C"],"acceptable":["r2B","r3A"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"col1 at 82px leaves 61px of text — just under the 60px four-character service names — so 支付服务/消息推送/对象存储 all break into 2+2 syllables, turning the row-label column into a ragged stack while the 1–2px needed to fix it sit idle in 可用率/最近事件."},{"design":"r1C","why":"Same fault, one pixel worse: at 81px every four-character service name wraps, so the reader can no longer take the leftmost column in one glance and rows lose their anchoring label."},{"design":"r3B","why":"Giving 服务 108px to one-line 'API Gateway' steals 25px from 最近事件, crushing the prose column to 80px — events now run 6 lines, 2-word fragments per line ('慢，已切换/至备用通道'), the table grows to 521px and the event text, the actual payload, becomes the hardest thing to read."},{"design":"r3C","why":"col1 82px still splits the service names, and the extra width handed to 状态 (78) buys nothing while 最近事件 drops to 124px, pushing one event to 5 lines and the table to 451px — worse on both axes than r2A."}],"contrast":{"widths":[95,60,75,129],"why":"Plausible-looking ('give the label column room, trim the chatter'), but it over-funds 服务 by 12px that no string needs while 状态/可用率 keep their minimum and 最近事件 loses a line of measure, making the event prose noticeably more chopped than r2A for no gain anywhere."},"ranges":[[83,95],[55,80],[75,88],[116,128]],"rationale":"The table has two jobs: identify the service (a fixed short label) and explain what happened (variable prose). The label column therefore only needs to clear 83px — enough for four Chinese characters on one line — and every pixel beyond that is taken directly from the only column that actually wants space. 状态 and 可用率 are compact, one-line, fixed-format fields (icon+word, percentage) that must simply not wrap; they need ~75px each and no more, which is exactly what r2A/r2C give them. 最近事件 then gets ~105px of measure, keeping events at 4 lines and the table at 428px, which is the tightest readable version. The 1px variations among r2A/r2B/r2C are visually indistinguishable; the real fault line is at col1 = 82, where service names split and the whole left edge starts to crumble.","principles":{"general":["A short-identifier column's width is set by its longest full entry, not by its longest word: the Chinese four-character names and 'API Gateway' define two different targets (83 vs 108), and paying for the second is usually a bad trade against a prose column.","Compact fixed-format columns (status, percentage) need exactly 'header or value + padding' and nothing more; slack given there is stolen from the flexible prose column.","Break a label column only if the alternative costs a lot elsewhere — a 2px shortfall that splits every row label is a worse defect than a slightly narrow text column, because it damages the reader's row-anchoring.","In narrow widths, one extra line in a prose column is cheap; one extra line in the label column multiplied by every row is expensive in scannability."],"specific":["Service names are all exactly four characters (60px), so 服务 is a step function: 83px = one line, 82px = two lines for three of five rows.","可用率's header (54px) and its values are the same width, so 75px is a hard floor with no reason to exceed it.","The emoji-led 最近事件 entries (clock, family, flags) can break anywhere, so that column tolerates narrow measure better than 服务 does — but only up to a point;
